system:
You evolve bot policies for a programming competition. A policy is a genome: a set of genes
(small typed functions) in the gene language below. The fixed loop lists every legal option each turn,
calls score(o) on each, and does the best one while its score is > 0.

# The game
Cambridge Battlecode 2026a. Two teams of 3-5 champions on a grid map (30x30 to 100x100).
Camps (wolves, elks, golems, gem/gold clusters, monoliths) sit on the map; damaging one wakes
its group, which then attacks the nearest champion. Killing every monster in a group and then
standing on one of its tiles for 5 rounds captures its gold and gems. Carried gems become score
only when tributed beside an altar (a channel of ceil(gems/10) turns; stun cancels it). A dead
champion drops its carried gems to its killer and sits out 60 rounds. First team to tribute
1000 gems wins; otherwise after 2000 rounds the team with more tributed gems wins.
Gold buys shards on your spawn (30 gold each; 5 of one stat combine into an emblem). Each turn a
champion may walk one tile, basic attack once (melee range 1, ranged 3; ranged champions cannot
do both in one turn), and cast one of two abilities (8-turn cooldowns). Recall (5 turns,
cancelled by damage) teleports home; standing on spawn heals. Vision is 8 tiles, blocked by
walls and bushes, and is not shared between allies; 8 bytes of shared memory are.
Every operation and engine call a bot runs costs fuel; each bot gets 100,000 fuel per turn, and a bot that runs
out is suspended mid-turn and loses tempo. So cheaper policies are better, all else equal.
Observations from today's top-12 ladder games (current rules), for inspiration, not rules:
- Long games (median ~1,100 rounds); more gems captured predicts the winner 92%, more gold 86%,
  more kills 79%, fewer deaths 76%. Wards, altar locks and teleports show no effect.
- Monoliths: the team capturing more wins ~80% where they exist. Top teams never go alone
  (success 0% solo, 29% with 2, 49% with 3, 69% with 4 attackers), start after ~round 1,000,
  commit ~30 rounds, recall individually at low health and return, abandon below 2 attackers.
  (In our tests a plain "3 allies go to the monolith after round 1,000" rule lost badly, so it
  probably needs more damage/sustain first.)
- Drafts: Vesper Vale, Heart of Ruin, Marcella, Vendetta, Ryth. Heart of Ruin plays normally
  (recall ~40-45% health, shield on cooldown in fights, dash toward goals or onto camps).
- Builds: Treasure shards early, then Bruiser (Power Strength for Vesper Vale).
In a genome, compiled gene code is cheap (a few fuel per operation); engine calls (distance fields
via field(), vision queries such as enemies()/camps()) cost more. A turn over budget is suspended.

# The gene language
# Gene language reference

Generated from `genome/lang.py` (`python3 -m genome.reference > genome/LANGUAGE.md`). Design: `docs/GENOME.md`.

## A genome file

Python syntax, restricted to a typed subset. Top level: keep declarations and genes only.

```python
BAG: Num = 20                      # keep: persistent per bot instance; only update() assigns it
GOALS: Field = None                # keeps: Num, Bool, Tile (starts invalid), Tiles and Field (start empty)

@gene("g7", "danger at a tile", parents=["g2"])
def danger_at(t: Tile) -> Num:
    return sum(u.strength * u.health_frac for u in enemies() if dist(u.pos, t) <= 5)
```

- Entry genes: `score(o: Option) -> Num` (required): the value of doing option `o` now; the fixed loop does the best option while its score is > 0 (the draft always picks). `update() -> None` (optional): runs at the start of each turn; the only gene that may assign keeps or call `write_shared` / `set_priority`. `consider(kind: Num) -> Bool` (optional): option kinds it rejects are neither listed nor scored this pass. `reserve() -> Num` (optional, default 15000): read once per turn after `update()`; the loop starts no pass after the first with less fuel left than this (a turn that runs out of fuel is suspended and the next turn is lost).
- `after() -> None` (optional entry gene): runs at the end of each turn, after the loop's actions, with fresh observations. Like `update()`, it may assign keeps and call `write_shared` / `set_priority`. `acted(kind)` and `acted_tile(kind)` tell it what the loop did this turn (e.g. announce the camp it attacked, so allies acting later in the round see it). Shared bytes written in one gene and read in another are dependency edges, as calls are.
- Keeps: `Num`, `Bool`, `Tile`, `Tiles`, `Field`. Use a Tiles/Field keep set in `update()` to compute an expensive set or distance field once per turn instead of once per pass (zero-argument genes are recomputed every pass of the loop).
- Every gene has `@gene(id, description, parents=[...])`. IDs survive inheritance; a duplicated gene gets a new ID.
  IDs and parent IDs are 1-64 of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . -`; a description is one plain line (no control, format or
  line-separator characters, no backslash), since both are emitted into C++ `//` comments.
- Statements: assignment (function-scoped locals, type fixed at first assignment), `+= -= *= /=`, `if/elif/else`, `for x in S` (S: Units, Tiles or `range(n)`), `return`.
- Expressions: arithmetic on Num (`/` by 0 gives 0), comparisons, `and/or/not`, `a if c else b`, `t in S` (Tile in Tiles), Tiles `| & -`, fields (`u.pos`), calls to genes and primitives.
- Reductions: `sum(e for x in S if c)`, `count(c for x in S)`, `any(...)`, `all(...)`, `max((e for x in S), default=d)` (Python needs the generator in parentheses next to `default=`), `min(...)`, `max(a, b)`, `min(a, b)`; `best(S, lambda x: score)` returns the element with the highest score (an invalid Unit/Tile if S is empty: test with `exists(u)` / `valid(t)`).
- No recursion, no other loops: every gene finishes. Zero-argument genes are computed once per pass of the loop.
- Fuel: each own operation is charged (placeholder price until calibrated); primitives that call the engine are charged as the engine call. A turn over budget is suspended, as in the real game.

Option kinds: PICK (o.champ), MOVE (o.tile), ATTACK (o.unit), CAST (o.slot + o.unit or o.tile), WARD (o.tile), BUY (o.item, o.count: 1, 2, 4, ... units up to what we can pay), BUY_LOCK (on spawn or dead), RECALL, TRIBUTE (o.tile = altar; at an enemy-locked altar it hits the lock), CANCEL (a running recall/tribute), LOCK (o.tile = altar), BREAK (o.tile = an enemy altar lock's altar within attack range, while we can attack; o.unit invalid: a basic attack on the lock, 5 clear it), TELEPORT (o.tile within 3, landable as a move: starts a teleport crystal's 3-turn channel; listed while we hold a crystal), BUY_TP (a teleport crystal: on spawn or dead), SELL (o.item: Tavi on spawn, one sale per turn, full refund).

Notes on the newer primitives (SDK reads and generic operations only):
- `vision()`, `ally_tiles()`, `enemy_tiles()`, `camp_tiles()`: the SDK's vision and occupancy masks (one engine call each). `ally_tiles()` includes me.
- `field_avoid(goals, walls, stop)`: the engine distance field to `goals` over tiles not in `walls`; the search ends after the layer by which every reachable `stop` tile has been reached (the host's ComputeTo; one stop tile: the first layer that reaches it; empty `stop`: whole map), farther tiles read unreachable (1e9).
- `box_field(goals, walls)`: the walking field to `goals` over tiles not in `walls`, through the engine field memo the policy bot's walking uses (cheap on later turns while the goals stay the same); readable only on my 3 x 3 box and up to my own distance (enough to choose a step), unreachable (1e9) everywhere else.
- `dash_field(goal, walls)`: the walking field to one `goal` tile through the engine field memo the policy bot's dash uses (root = the goal, dests = my 5 x 5 box); only the box tiles nearest to the goal read their distance, every other tile unreachable (1e9): for choosing a dash landing. ~4-6k per call.
- `wfield(goals, walls, slow, k)`: a weighted walking field computed in our own code (Dijkstra, bucket queue): stepping onto a tile costs 1, or 1 + k on a `slow` tile (k clamped to 0..8); `walls` cannot be entered (goal tiles can); distances above 65534 read 1e9. Dear: a whole 100x100 map costs ~4.5M fuel in the bot (~45 turns of budget), 90x30 ~1.3M.
- `path_step(from, to, walls, budget)` / `path_len(...)`: A* from `from` to `to` over tiles not in `walls` (`to` allowed), expanding at most `budget` tiles: the first step (invalid if not found) / the length (1e9). About 1.4k + 380 per tile expanded in the bot.
- `territory(mine, theirs, walls)`: tiles strictly nearer by walking to `mine` than to `theirs` (empty `theirs`: every tile reachable from `mine`), over tiles not in `walls` (sources allowed): two engine fields and a compare in our code, ~300k fuel on 100x100 (~80k on 90x30).
- Fights, exact from the game's formulas and the units' host data (emblem passives from their items, shields from their buffs), in the engine's float order: `attack_damage(a, b)` what one basic attack of `a` takes off `b` (strength, missing-health passive, Monster emblem and the camp multiplier against camps, then Durability / Jungle; before shields); `cast_damage(a, slot, b)` the same for a damage / stun / area ability (modifier x focus); `shield(u)` the shield left on a champion. A champion's items and buffs are read once per pass (~0.9k); calls ~0.1-0.25k after that.
- Raw unit reads (the SDK's data, no judgement; 0 for a unit out of vision): `cooldown(u, s)` turns left on slot s (a champion's ability; a camp's attack 0 / ability 1); `ability_*(u, s)` a champion's ability design on slot s (kind, base cooldown, range, radius, target mask, modifier, duration, moveless), any champion; `item_count(u, i)` copies of item i a visible champion owns; `unit_gold(u)`; `buff_value(u, t)` / `buff_turns(u, t)` buffs of type t (0 shield, 1 stun, 2 enhanced attack) on a champion or camp: summed shield amount (the number of buffs for other types) / longest duration left; `channel_left(u)` turns left on a recall / gem submission / teleport channel; `group_cooldown(g)` turns until camp group g respawns; `lock_hits(t)` / `lock_enemy(t)` a visible altar lock on tile t: hits left (0 none) / it is the enemy's. 20-230 fuel each in the bot; records (items, buffs, ability design, a camp's record, the lock list) are fetched once per unit per pass, later reads ~20-60.
- Wards, sight, teleports, turn order (raw reads): `ally_wards()` / `enemy_wards()` visible wards' tiles (~1.2k, once per pass); `ward_charges()` / `ward_cooldown()` my ward charges and turns to the next; `my_ward()` my placed ward (invalid if none); `ward_sight(t)` what a ward at t would see, `sight(k, t)` what a champion of type k at t would see (~0.4k + the board); `teleport_dest(u)` / `teleport_left(u)` a visible teleport in flight (invalid / 0 if none); `priority(u)` a visible champion's turn priority this round; `can_sell()`.
- `walk_nearest(cand, from, walls)`: the engine's nearest-by-walk (ties row-major); invalid if none is reachable.
- `type_spawns(k)`, `spawn_type(t)`, `spawn_group(t)`, `camp_spawn(u)`, `camp_base_*(k)`: static map and camp design data (-1 off a spawn tile).
- `is_awake(u)`: camp life state; `group_reward(g)`: the group is cleared and waiting for capture.
- `set_priority(p)`: turn order for the next round (update() only). `rand(n)`: uniform integer in [0, n) from the instance's own generator.

Also: `consider(kind: Num) -> Bool` (optional entry gene) is asked once per option kind each pass;
kinds it rejects are neither listed nor scored, which saves the fuel of listing and scoring them.
Expensive sets and distance fields can be computed once per turn into a Tiles/Field keep in update()
instead of in a zero-argument gene (recomputed every pass of the loop). A mutation may add consider(),
update() or after() if the genome has none.
Pathfinding in our own code is expensive, so use it rarely or locally: wfield() over a whole 100x100 map costs
~4.5M fuel (~45 turns of budget; 90x30 ~1.3M), so cache it in a Field keep from update() every N turns; path_step()
/ path_len() (A*) cost ~1.4k + 380 per tile expanded: ~10-20k for a local path with budget ~400 near a camp or
altar, 1-4.5M across the map. territory(mine, theirs, walls) (tiles strictly nearer by walking to `mine` than to
`theirs`) costs ~300k on 100x100 (~80k on 90x30): cache it in a Tiles keep from update().
Fight reads (attack_damage, cast_damage, shield) are exact: per visible enemy, the damage reads both ways cost ~1.3k
fuel on the first call in a pass and ~0.4k after.
Team coordination: the 8 shared bytes (read_shared anywhere; write_shared in update() or after()) are the only
channel between allies; vision is not shared. after() can announce what this champion just did.
